title: Regular Polygons Practice
description: Practice identifying regular and irregular polygons using equal sides and equal angles.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a regular polygon?
options: It has at least one pair of equal sides.
It has all sides equal and all interior angles equal.
It has all sides equal but angles can be different.
It has all angles equal but sides can be different.
questions.explanation: A regular polygon must pass both tests: all side lengths are equal and all interior angles are equal.

questions.question: A pentagon has side lengths 5 cm, 5 cm, 5 cm, 5 cm, and 5 cm. Its angles are 108°, 108°, 108°, 108°, and 108°. How should it be classified?
questions.explanation: The shape has 5 sides, so it is a pentagon. All sides and all angles match, so it is regular.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has four equal sides but its angle measures are 70°, 110°, 70°, and 110°. Is it regular?
options: Yes, because all four sides are equal.
Yes, because opposite angles are equal.
No, because the angles are not all equal.
No, because regular polygons cannot have 4 sides.
questions.explanation: Equal sides alone are not enough. A regular polygon must also have all interior angles equal.

questions.question: A polygon can be irregular even if it has the same number of sides as a regular polygon.
questions.explanation: Regularity is based on equal side lengths and equal angle measures, not just the number of sides.

questions.question: Which tool is most useful for checking whether the sides of a drawn polygon are equal?
questions.explanation: A ruler measures side lengths, so it helps check whether the sides are equal.

questions.question: Which tool is most useful for checking whether the interior angles of a drawn polygon are equal?
questions.explanation: A protractor measures angles, so it helps compare interior angle measures.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: A polygon with all sides equal and all angles equal is called a ______ polygon.
questions.explanation: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal.

questions.question: A hexagon has all six angles equal, but one side is longer than the others. Explain whether it is regular.
questions.correctAnswer: It is not regular because a regular polygon must have all sides equal and all angles equal. This hexagon fails the equal-side test.
questions.explanation: Even though the angles match, the unequal side length makes the hexagon irregular.
